sentences.text: This petition under Section 166 MV Act is filed by the Petitioner seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. It is the specific case of the petitioner that on 07-12-2022 at about 6.30 p.m., he was walking along the side of the road near Harohalli Lake, Harohalli Town, Harohalli Hobli, Ramanagara District.

At that time, the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No. KA-04-JV-0940 (hereinafter referred to as the "offending vehicle") rode the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and at a high speed and dashed against the petitioner.
3. As a result of the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately shifted to Chandramma Dayananda Sagar Hospital, where he was given first aid, and thereafter referred to Nimhan's Hospital.
Upon further examination, he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru, where he was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
4. The petitioner has contended that he incurred huge expenditure towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
It is further contended that at the time of the accident, the petitioner was aged about 57 years and was working as a coolie, earning 18,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner has suffered permanent disability and is unable to lead a normal life as he did prior to the accident.
On account of such permanent disability, he has suffered loss of earning capacity and loss of income.

5. As the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle, the petitioner has sought compensation from Respondent No. 1, the insurer of the offending vehicle, and Respondent No. 2, the owner of the offending vehicle.
6. In response to the petition, upon service of notice, the respondent No.1 appeared before this Court through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Respondent No. 2 has failed to appear before the court and placed exparte.
7. Respondent No. 1 has admitted the issuance of the insurance policy covering the offending vehicle and that the same was in force as on the date of the accident.

However, it is pleaded that its liability,
if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

It is further contended that the mandatory provisions under Section 133(c) and Section 158(6) of the Motor Vehicles Act were not complied with by either the owner of the motorcycle or the police authorities.
8. The insurer has denied the negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and contended that the rider did not possess a valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.
It has also denied the occurrence, the manner of the accident, and the involvement of the offending vehicle.

Further, the insurer has denied the nature of injuries, treatment taken, medical expenses Nagaraju vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20510934/
2 incurred, and the quantum of compensation claimed, contending that the claim is excessive and exaggerated, and has prayed for dismissal of the petition.
9.

sentences.text:
On the basis of the above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.Whether the petitioner proves that on 07-12-2022 at about 6.30 p.m., when he was pedestrian near Harohalli Lake, Harohalli Town, Harohalli Hobli, Ramanagar District, one motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA-04-JV-0940 came from behind with high speed in a rash and negligently, dashed against the petitioner, as a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, what amount?
3. What order or award?
10. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in support of his case, 2 witnesses were examined as PW-2 and 3 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.17.
On the other hand the Respondent No.1 got examined the AMRO of CDSIMER as RW.1 and got marked 3 documents as per Ex.R1 to 3.

Respondent No.1 has also examined its official as RW-2 and got marked the documents at Ex.R.4 and 5.
11.
I have heard the arguments of counsel for the Petitioner and respondents and have perused the material on record.

12. My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Negative. Issue No.2: In the Negative.
Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

REASONS 13. ISSUE NO.1: It is the case of the petitioner that on 07-12-2022 at about 6.30 p.m., while he was walking along the side of the road near Harohalli Lake, Harohalli Town, Harohalli Hobli,
Ramanagara District, the offending motorcycle came from behind at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against him, resulting in severe injuries to his right leg.
14. In order to substantiate his claim, the petitioner has filed his affidavit under Order XVIII Rule 4 of CPC and examined himself as PW-1.

He has reiterated the averments made in the petition and relied upon police documents marked as Exhibits P-1 to P-8, which include FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, notice, reply notice, IMV report, wound certificate, and charge sheet.
15. On perusal of Exhibit P-1 (FIR), it is evident that the accident is shown to have occurred on 07-12- 2022 at about 6.30 p.m. near the alleged place of occurrence.

The Exhibit P-2 (complaint)
indicates that the petitioner was walking by the side of the road and that the offending motorcycle Nagaraju vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20510934/
3 came at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against him.

sentences.text: However, a careful reading of the records reveals that though the accident allegedly occurred on 07-12-2022, the complaint was lodged on 13-12-2022, after a delay of six days.
16. Further, Exhibit P-4 discloses that the police issued a notice under Section 133 of the Motor Vehicles Act to the owner of the offending motorcycle.

In response thereto, the owner submitted a reply marked as Exhibit P-5, wherein it is specifically stated by the RC Owner of the motorcycle that the petitioner had requested for a lift and was travelling as a pillion rider on the motorcycle.

It is further stated therein that an Innova car, coming at high speed with high-beam lights on, dashed against the motorcycle, as a result of which he and the pillion rider i.e.,petitioner/ Nagaraj fell down and sustained injuries.
17. Exhibit P-6 (IMV report) shows that the motorcycle sustained damages on both the front and rear portions.
18. To further prove the manner of the accident, the petitioner examined an alleged eyewitness as PW-3.
PW-3 deposed that he witnessed the accident on 07- 12-2022 at about 6.30 p.m., wherein the offending motorcycle dashed against the petitioner who was walking by the side of the road.
However, during the course of cross-examination, PW-3 admitted that if any person witnesses an accident, there would be no difficulty in lodging a complaint immediately.
He also admitted that two persons sustained injuries in the accident and that he shifted the petitioner to Chandramma Dayananda Sagar Hospital.

19. The principal defence raised by Respondent No. 1 is that the accident was not solely attributable to the offending motorcycle and that the police, without conducting a fair and complete investigation, filed a charge sheet only against the rider of the motorcycle, despite clear indications of involvement of an Innova car.
It is further contended that the petitioner approached this Tribunal by suppressing material facts and misrepresenting his role in the accident.
To substantiate the same the official of Respondent no 1 was examined as RW2.
He has filed an affidavit under order XVIII rule IV in lieu of examination in chief and he reiterated the above said contention.
Therefore, the core issue for determination is whether the petitioner has proved the manner of accident and negligence as pleaded, on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
20. The petitioner pleaded that he was a going by the roadside and was hit by the motorcycle.
However, Exhibit P5, produced by the petitioner himself, records that he was travelling as a pillion rider on the motorcycle.
This document directly contradicts the pleaded version.
Further, Exhibit P8 charge sheet also records that the petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider.
These documents are contemporaneous and emanate from official sources.

This contradiction is not minor or explainable;
it goes to the very foundation of the petitioner's case regarding how the accident occurred.

21. The status of the petitioner at the time of accident, whether as a pedestrian or pillion rider is a material fact, as it determines the manner of accident, the question of negligence, and the liability of the parties.
By pleading that he was a going by the road side while documentary evidence shows he was a pillion rider, the petitioner has suppressed a material fact.

Such suppression materially Nagaraju vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20510934/
4 damages his case, as it undermines his credibility and disentitles him to the discretionary relief under the Motor Vehicles Act.

sentences.text: A claimant who approaches the Tribunal with inconsistent versions cannot seek benefit of doubt.
22. Respondent No. 1 examined RW1, the medical record officer of Chandramma Dhenanda Sagar Hospital, who produced the MLC extract and police intimation marked as Exhibits R2 and R3.
These records disclose that the petitioner was a pillion rider and that the accident occurred due to collision between a two-wheeler and a four-wheeler.
It is further recorded that the petitioner was brought to the hospital by the police immediately after the accident.
These contemporaneous records consistently contradict the petitioner's version of being a pedestrian hit by a motorcycle.
23. The reply notice issued by the owner of the motorcycle, which is part of the record, attributes the cause of the accident to rash and negligent driving of an Innova car.
This version is corroborated by the IMV report, which reveals damage to both the front and rear portions of the motorcycle, clearly indicating impact from another vehicle.
Despite such material, the investigation officer chose to file the charge sheet only against the rider of the motorcycle.
No explanation has been placed on record as to why the driver of the Innova car was neither investigated nor arrayed as an accused.
This omission materially affects the reliability of the charge sheet insofar as negligence is concerned.
24. It is evident from Exhibit R2 that the petitioner was brought to the hospital by the police immediately after the accident.
Despite police knowledge of the incident, the complaint came to be lodged only after a delay of six days.
No explanation has been offered for such delay.

While delay alone may not be fatal, when read in conjunction with contradictory versions and suppression of material facts, the unexplained delay assumes significance and weakens the petitioner's credibility.
25. Though PW3 was examined as an eyewitness, his testimony does not satisfactorily reconcile the contradictions emerging from Exhibits P5, P8, R2, and R3.
When oral evidence conflicts with contemporaneous documentary evidence, greater weight must be attached to documents prepared in the ordinary course of business.
Therefore, the oral testimony does not conclusively establish that the petitioner was a pedestrian at the time of the accident.

26. The petitioner relied upon the decisions in Ravi v. Badrinarayan (2011 ACJ 911) and Mallamma v. Balaji (ILR 2003 KAR 493) to contend that delay in lodging FIR and strict application of the Evidence Act should not defeat a motor accident claim.
These principles are not in dispute.

However, the present case does not fail merely on delay or technicalities but on suppression of material facts, contradictory versions, and documentary evidence disproving the pleaded manner of accident.
Hence, the facts of those decisions are clearly distinguishable and do not advance the petitioner's case.

27. On a cumulative assessment of Exhibits P5, P8, R2, R3, the reply notice of the owner, the IMV report, and the unexplained delay, it is evident that the petitioner has not come before the Tribunal with clean hands.
The suppression of his role as a pillion rider and the attempt to project himself as a pedestrian materially damages the trustworthiness of his case.
The contradictions strike at the root of the claim and create serious doubt regarding the manner of accident and negligence pleaded.

5 28. In motor accident claims, though strict proof is not required, the claimant must establish negligence on the scale of preponderance of probabilities.
In the present case, the petitioner has failed to prove that the accident occurred in the manner pleaded or that the rider of the offending motorcycle was solely negligent.
Accordingly , Issue No.1 is answered in the Negative.

29. Issue No.2: The petitioner has pleaded one version before this Tribunal, whereas the contemporaneous records disclose a materially different version regarding the manner of the accident and the role of the petitioner.
Such a fundamental inconsistency strikes at the root of the claim and seriously impairs the credibility of the petitioner.
The contradictory stands taken by the petitioner create a cloud of doubt over the bona fides of the claim and render the version put forth before this Tribunal unreliable.
30. When a claimant approaches the Tribunal with inconsistent pleadings that are not borne out by contemporaneous documentary evidence, the benefit of doubt cannot be extended in his favour.
In the present case, the petitioner has failed to establish the manner of accident and negligence as pleaded, even on the standard of preponderance of probabilities.
Accordingly, this Tribunal holds that the petitioner is not entitled to any compensation as sought under the present petition, and Issue No. 2 is answered in the negative.
31. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to above Issues,
I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is dismissed Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer typed by her corrected, signed and pronounced by me in open court dated this the 6th day of January 2026.)
